newsitem.title: UK: Gold Outlook - Market wary around $340 level.
newsitem.headline: Gold Outlook - Market wary around $340 level.

text.p: The gold market is due for more whippy, volatile trading this week following Friday's tumble to near four-year lows, dealers and analysts said.
The price drop on Friday to below $340 an ounce -- a psychologically important support level from 1993 -- set up $330 as the next downside target, analysts said.
Bullion fixed at $339.75 on Friday afternoon, the lowest fixing since April 22, 1993. It recovered from lows near $338 to close at $340.20/$340.80.
But before heading to fresh lows, prices were vulnerable to an upside correction or at least a consolidation period, several technical analysts said.
That meant sharp upside surges might be on the books in the near term despite the market's overwhelmingly downside bias.
"One thing's for sure -- we have volatility back in the market," a dealer noted.
"Gold is definitely being sold down with the market's eye on $332 as the target. But it could easily pop up to $346-$347 in the next few days."
Any correction would encounter continued selling from myriad sources, analysts said.

"We have seen selling from desperate investors who bought gold at remarkably high prices a long time ago and are more and more convinced that these prices will not be seen again in the medium term," said a senior analyst based in continental Europe.
Producer hedging and the threat of central bank selling would also keep bearish sentiment running at full steam, he added.
"I am more convinced than ever that central banks are in the market and selling since Eurostat ruled that they could sell gold and use the revenue to reduce debt," the analyst said.
But whether or not a central bank was selling or not was almost secondary, he said.
"It is not so much the fact of selling as the market's perception that selling might be happening that is the problem," the dealer added.
The other precious metals were also displaying increasing volatility.
Silver attacked both the highs and lows of its recent $4.80-$5.00 range on Friday, ending at $4.93/$4.95 in London.
Palladium was at six-month highs above $130 due to speculative and consumer buying on concerns about delayed Russian exports.
Platinum was hovering just above and below its key $350 level and keeping an eye on gold for further direction.
